evidence: 0095 (B4, owner decisions of 2026-10-28, patient sharing; migrations pre-approved for this batch, unsigned until the lead signs) is additive. New tables, each under forced RLS with an owner policy only and no grant (only the new SECURITY DEFINER commands touch them): identity.patient_share_invitations (a patient's invitation to an address, lowercased, 3-254 characters, one @; an optional name, never emailed; level view_only, clinical_review or clinical_collaboration; duration 24h, 7d, 30d or until_revoked; an 8-character reference; status pending, accepted, confirmed, cancelled or expired with a CHECK per status; the accepting membership and account; the grant it became; delivery_outcome pending, sent, failed or not_sent; Idempotency-Key and request digest unique per patient; one open invitation per patient and address; 30 days; a guard trigger keeps identity fields fixed, closed statuses terminal and an acceptance unchanged, and refuses deletes); identity.patient_consent_shares (per grant made by a patient share or a confirmed invitation: membership, level, duration, origin, the share it replaced, the key; immutable); identity.record_access_notices (one row per patient, facility and Africa/Lagos day: the grant, access kind standard, share or pin, the inbox item and the email state pending, delivered, failed, not_sent or suppressed with lease and retry; no delete). 20 new SECURITY DEFINER functions with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp, every body PL/pgSQL: the patient commands bound to identity.patient_self_session (42501 without a live session): search_share_providers (3-80 characters, % _ \ escaped, a contains-match on clinician, facility or organisation name, at most 25 eligible memberships: name, role, facility, organisation and a new flag; audit with the count only), create_my_consent_share (under 0087's advisory key patient-access-pin:<patient>; Idempotency-Key replay or 55000 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; P0001 past 20 shares a day; P0002 for a membership that is unknown, not eligible or the patient's own; a consent_grants row with request_id null, granted_by_patient_id the patient, purpose direct-care, view_only and clinical_review read_records, clinical_collaboration write_records, starts now, until_revoked 365 days; the side row; the earlier active patient share to that membership revoked 'Replaced by a new share' in the same transaction), list_my_share_invitations, create_my_share_invitation (reads no workforce table and no account, so the answer is the same whether or not the address is registered; 409 ALREADY_OPEN and TOO_MANY_OPEN at 20 open, P0001 past 5 a day, past 3 emails a day to one address across all patients the invitation is created unsent), record_my_share_invitation_delivery, cancel_my_share_invitation, confirm_my_share_invitation (only an accepted, unexpired offer whose membership is still eligible and still signs in with the invited verified address; the grant is written as by a share); the staff commands bound to the request's subject, membership and facility with direct-care: list_shared_with_me (identity.consent.write; the active shares to the caller's membership with the patient's Health ID and name), list_share_invitations_for_me (the pending invitations to the caller's verified sign-in email, no patient identity; eligible false and no items for an ineligible membership), accept_share_invitation (P0002 unless addressed to the caller's verified email, 42501 SHARE_PROVIDER_NOT_ELIGIBLE, 55000 unless pending; enqueues SHARE_INVITATION_ACCEPTED with the facility name); note_record_access (an active, unexpired, non-break-glass grant of the caller's membership, facility and account; one notice per patient, facility and Lagos day, at most 10 a day; RECORDS_OPENED with facilityName and accessKind; the email pending only for 0063's verified recipient); system:auth only: expire_share_invitations (SHARE_INVITATION_EXPIRED), claim_record_access_alerts (SKIP LOCKED, lease 15-600 s, recipient re-checked, at most 5 attempts within 24 hours) and record_record_access_alert_outcome; internal and granted to no role: share_provider_eligible (an active membership, an unrevoked facility doctor, clinician or nurse role, identity.consent.write, and a self-service state of none or reviewed), share_provider_role, share_staff_actor, write_patient_share, close_expired_share_invitations, share_audit, and the guard trigger function. Every write and committed refusal records its audit.events row with ids, codes and counts only. Replaced body, pinned by md5 of pg_proc.prosrc before (0087's 7d5b6361e7afb2d417b4d1beef577e79) and after (0aef8026c24f923c1612280447f99b66): identity.patient_self_access_history, 0087's body with three keys added to each item, shareLevel, shareDuration and clinicianName (null unless the grant came from a share or a confirmed invitation); every 0087 key, the limit and the order unchanged; owner, ACL, language, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path post-checked. Preconditions (55000, nothing applied): prerequisites exist; no object of 0095 exists (already applied); the replaced body and 17 relied-on bodies (the request-context readers, identity.patient_self_session, has_active_membership, membership_has_permission, has_active_consent_grant, the inbox enqueue, 0087's revoke, facility_self_service_state, self_service_on_probation, organization_self_service_state, verified_notification_recipient, the audit trigger and platform.reject_mutation) pinned by md5; the consent_grants scope, status, expiry, revoked-pair, break-glass, grantor, authorization-method and PIN-scope CHECKs, access_requests' authorization method and the inbox's code, resource type and metadata CHECKs pinned by definition; the applying role owns identity.patients and identity.consent_grants (both have row-level security) and the replaced function, and holds SELECT on the workforce tables, auth.accounts, identity.facilities, identity.organizations and identity.organization_applications, INSERT on audit.events, CREATE on schema identity and EXECUTE on every function called, by ownership, membership or grant and never a superuser's bypass (42501 otherwise). Locks: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on identity.patients and identity.consent_grants (the new foreign keys), taken up front, NOWAIT every 10 ms for at most 5 s (then 55P03, nothing applied), held to commit: they block writes to those tables, never reads. Measured with pg_locks before commit: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and ACCESS SHARE on those two tables, ACCESS SHARE on their primary keys; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the three new tables, their indexes and TOAST tables; ACCESS SHARE on platform.reject_mutation and the guard trigger function; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on four new functions (comments); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the migration's own temporary table and helper and the session's temporary schema; no lock on any other application table (none on audit.events, auth.accounts, the workforce tables, notification.inbox_items or identity.facilities) and none on the replaced function. With a write held open on identity.consent_grants, and again on identity.patients, the runner stopped after 5.3-5.5 s with 55P03 and nothing applied, then applied once it ended. Grants: the 14 commands to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, nothing to hid_ehr_runtime, every new function revoked from PUBLIC, no grant on any table, in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql; the replaced function keeps its ACL. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with the repository's runner, as the pgrun user: 0001-0094 applied and roles bootstrapped, then 0095 planned, dry-run and applied (71-97 ms over two runs; 28 function grants from the migration itself), a rerun found 0 pending, the file applied again stopped with 55000 0095: already applied, the role bootstrap and verify-roles passed; a fresh database took 0001-0095 in one dry run and one apply; a copy whose schemas, tables and functions belong to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner applied 0095 as that owner; copies with a drifted relied-on body (self_service_on_probation) or a dropped consent_grants_pin_scope_ck, and an applying role that does not own identity.consent_grants, stopped with nothing applied. All 16 database/tests and 53 test/database suites pass on the upgraded and the fresh copy, among them the three new suites patient-sharing (security properties and grants; the eligibility matrix with a governed facility, a facility on probation (new), a pending self-service facility, a lab scientist, a revoked role, an inactive membership and the patient's own membership; escaping, the 3-80 limits and the 25-candidate cap; every level and duration and the 365-day horizon; replacement; write implying read through has_active_consent_grant; 0087's revoke of a share; the history's keys; Idempotency-Key replay and reuse; the 20-a-day limit; another session refused; the staff list), patient-share-invitations (the create body reads no workforce table or account and answers a registered and an unregistered address alike; replay, key reuse, an open duplicate, invalid addresses; 5 a day; 20 open; 3 emails a day per address with the fourth unsent and not_confirmed; delivery outcomes; the invitee list without patient identity; acceptance refused for another address, an unverified email and an ineligible membership; SHARE_INVITATION_ACCEPTED; confirm before and after acceptance, replay, not cancellable once confirmed; cancel after accept with no grant; expiry read before the sweep, the system-only sweep and SHARE_INVITATION_EXPIRED; the guard trigger) and record-access-notices (one notice per facility and Lagos day, 10 a day then capped, break-glass, ended, other-facility and other-membership grants not applicable, kinds standard, share and pin, no email without a verified recipient, RECORDS_OPENED metadata, audit rows; claim and outcome system-only, the lease, stale leases, retry backoff, the 24-hour window, a recipient who turned notifications off), and the changed patient-grant-revocation suite (the history's three new keys); six definer suites pass with the NOSUPERUSER owner. Old images on this schema: the previous Identity calls none of the new functions and reads none of the new tables; its access history passes the three new keys through (publishAccessHistory spreads every key) and the previous website ignores them; EHR, Lab, Pharmacy and Notification are untouched. Applied migrations 0001-0094 are unchanged. 0096 (B5, owner decisions of 2026-10-28, delete my account; main's 0064 lifecycle ported; migrations pre-approved for this batch) is additive. New tables, each with forced row-level security, an owner policy only and no grant: platform.record_class_retention_policies (seven record classes, retain only, never an automatic purge), platform.legal_holds (released, never deleted or rewritten: a guard trigger), platform.patient_account_deletion_settings (14 days, 10 minutes, 5 requests a day, 5 attempts), identity.patient_account_deletion_requests (main's lifecycle; one open request per login; only the confirmation token's SHA-256; no foreign key to auth.sessions; never deleted) and identity.patient_account_deletion_notices (the scheduled, cancelled and completed emails, their lease and retry; never deleted). A trigger accounts_deleted_terminal on auth.accounts, WHEN old.status = 'deleted', keeps a deleted login deleted, without a password, with its token version and subject. Replaced: identity.current_patient_account(text) and identity.patient_self_session(text,uuid), 0030's bodies (md5-pinned) with identity.patient_account_deletion_due(a.id) appended as main, created with check_function_bodies off so that the apply reads no table; every other attribute (owner, ACL, language sql, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER, search_path, result) is recorded before and compared after, and the new bodies are compared by md5. Eleven SECURITY DEFINER functions with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp: status, request, confirm and cancel bound to identity.patient_self_session; the finalizer (SKIP LOCKED, 1-50), the email claim and the outcome bound to system:auth; completion (internal) revokes sessions (patient_account_deleted, a session event each), federated links, the access PIN under 0087's advisory lock, patient-granted grants (approvals, PIN grants and 0095's shares; never break-glass), expires pending access requests, revokes notification devices, deactivates emergency contacts (account_deleted, the contact erased as 0084's CHECK requires), cancels open share invitations, invalidates a pending contact change (contact_unavailable, the new contact erased), suppresses pending records-opened emails and sets the account deleted without a password; every record class is kept. Legal holds and workforce accounts (a staff record, an unrevoked role or any facility membership) block, at confirmation and again at finalization. Inbox: ACCOUNT_DELETION_SCHEDULED, ACCOUNT_DELETION_CANCELLED and ACCOUNT_DELETION_BLOCKED (resource account-deletion). Preconditions (catalog reads only): every prerequisite (0001-0095), the already-applied guard, md5 of the two replaced bodies and of six relied-on bodies (the request context readers, the inbox enqueue, the share invitation guard, the audit trigger, the no-delete trigger), 36 CHECKs pinned by pg_get_constraintdef (sessions, session events, accounts, federated links, the PIN, grants, access requests, device registrations, emergency contacts, contact changes, share invitations, records-opened notices, the inbox), and the applying role's privileges without a superuser's bypass (owner of the six RLS tables completion writes, named by the owner policies of the three with forced RLS, and owner of the two replaced functions; UPDATE, REFERENCES and TRIGGER on auth.accounts; the other writes and reads; CREATE in auth, identity and platform; EXECUTE on the functions called). Locks: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.accounts and identity.patients (the foreign keys and the trigger), taken up front in 0094's order, NOWAIT every 10 ms for at most 5 seconds, then 55P03 with nothing applied; measured with pg_locks before commit: those two, ACCESS SHARE on their primary keys, the new objects, the trigger functions, the catalogs; no lock on auth.sessions, audit.events, identity.consent_grants, the workforce tables, notification.inbox_items, the 0094 and 0095 tables or the replaced functions. Grants, in the migration and repeated in runtime-grants.sql: EXECUTE on the seven commands to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime; none on the due check, evaluation, completion, audit helper or trigger functions; none on any table; none to hid_ehr_runtime; the replaced functions keep their ACLs. Measured on the throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster as pgrun: 0001-0095 applied and roles bootstrapped, then 0096 planned, dry-run and applied by the runner (75 ms; 14 function grants from the migration itself), a rerun found 0 pending, the file applied again stopped with 55000 0096: already applied, the role bootstrap and verify-only passed; a fresh database took 0001-0096 in one dry run and one apply; a copy owned by a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner applied 0096 as that owner; copies with a drifted replaced body (patient_self_session), a dropped patient_emergency_contacts_check4, an applying role that does not own identity.access_requests, and a copy re-owned without rewriting the 0094 and 0095 owner policies (so they would not admit the applier) stopped with nothing applied; a write held on auth.accounts or identity.patients stopped the runner after 5.3-5.4 s with 55P03 and nothing applied, and it applied once the write ended. All 70 suites (16 in database/tests, 54 in test/database) pass on the upgraded and the fresh copy, among them the new test/database/patient-account-deletion.integration.sql (main's suite ported, plus 0093's workforce test with a revoked and an unrevoked platform role, the closures of emergency contacts, share invitations, a 0095 share grant, a pending contact change and records-opened emails, the inbox notices, cancelling before confirmation telling nothing, the deletion emails' claim, recipient, request_closed and no_recipient, outcome and lease, the terminal trigger, no address or token digest in any audit row) and the changed order-routes-cannot-complete suite (it pins every function the D18 bodies reach: now 0096's patient_self_session and the due check); nine definer suites pass with the NOSUPERUSER owner; four mutants of 0096 (invitations not cancelled, the staff record ignored by the workforce test, a revoked role blocking, the login usable after scheduled_for) each fail the deletion suite (a membership-only mutant is equivalent: every membership has a staff record of its account by foreign key). Old images on this schema: the previous Identity calls none of the new functions and reads none of the new tables; the replaced resolvers answer as before for any account with no due deletion, and none can be scheduled before the new Identity serves the routes; the trigger fires only for an account already deleted, which no current code changes; EHR, Lab, Pharmacy and Notification are untouched.
